summary: Iteration 17 backend verification for the new frontend Edit-Customer screen. The frontend consumes the EXISTING endpoint PUT /api/customers/{customer_id} (server.py L300-314). Added TestCustomerEditPUT (12 new tests) covering: (a) auth — 401 without JWT; (b) 404 for well-formed but non-existent ObjectId with Arabic detail 'المشترك غير موجود'; (c) 400 for malformed ObjectId with Arabic detail 'معرّف غير صالح'; (d) individual field updates (meter_number, phone, area, generator_id, address, name, notes, previous_balance) — each PUT is followed by an independent GET /api/customers/{id} to verify persistence; (e) all-fields-together update; (f) updated_at is refreshed after PUT (sleep 1.1s to guarantee monotonic ISO diff); (g) editing a customer does NOT mutate its existing invoices/readings; (h) amperage never leaks in the response. Full regression suite: 117/117 PASSED (100%) in ~27s. No new backend code was added — this is purely verification of an existing endpoint being reused by a new UI. No regressions across auth, customers, generators, readings, invoices, payments, expenses, dashboard, reports, cascade-delete, suspend, or reset-readings.

minor.issue: Accepts CustomerCreate (full replacement) rather than a partial CustomerUpdate model. The edit UI must always send every field; forgetting one (e.g., notes) will overwrite it with None. Consider a PATCH-style model with all-optional fields, or a dedicated CustomerUpdate model, so the frontend can send only the changed fields.

No uniqueness check on meter_number. Two customers can end up with the same meter_number via edit even though POST /customers doesn't explicitly enforce it either. Recommend a unique index on customers.meter_number plus a friendly 409 handler.

generator_id is not validated to exist. Sending a random string succeeds (Pydantic only sees a str). If a bad generator_id is stored, downstream joins may silently produce empty results. Recommend validating generator existence before $set.

Changing generator_id does NOT update generator.subscriber_count on either the old or the new generator. If the edit UI eventually allows moving a customer between generators, subscriber_count will drift. Not exercised by current UI, but flagged.
No amount>0 / phone-format validation. Sends '' for phone/address/meter_number are accepted.
(carried) All CustomerCreate-typed writes silently accept and drop 'amperage'; still verified as removed from responses.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Introduce a dedicated CustomerUpdate Pydantic model with all-optional fields so the frontend edit screen can send only changed fields (partial update) without wiping the untouched ones.
OPTIONAL: Add a unique index on customers.meter_number and return a friendly 409 when the edit screen tries to reuse an existing meter number.
OPTIONAL: Validate generator_id exists in db.generators on PUT; if generator_id changes, decrement old and increment new generator.subscriber_count atomically.
OPTIONAL: Add basic phone/meter_number format validators to CustomerCreate/CustomerUpdate to reject empty strings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L300-314 update_customer: correctly requires JWT (via api_router dependency), replaces the customer doc with the incoming CustomerCreate payload plus a fresh updated_at, returns 404 with Arabic detail when no doc matches, and relies on the global InvalidId handler to convert malformed ObjectId into 400 (verified).

Because the endpoint uses CustomerCreate (not a partial model), the frontend edit form MUST resend every field. This is a footgun worth documenting on the frontend side or refactoring to CustomerUpdate.

No side-effects on invoices/readings/payments/generators. Confirmed by test_put_does_not_affect_related_invoices_or_readings and by the generator subscriber_count remaining unchanged during PUT operations.
seed_data_creation: None. Each test creates TEST_EDIT_* customers and cleans them up in a finally block via DELETE /api/customers/{id} (which cascades readings/invoices/payments).
